title: Create a "Bootcamp Director's ROI Calculator"
description: Bootcamps care about efficiency. Zedu claims 50% faster mentor responses and 40% less admin overhead. Create a landing page copy or guide that walks a director through calculating their current admin costs vs. using Zedu.

acceptedWorkstreams.title: A calculator driven by the director's own numbers, with Zedu's real prices and no unsourced savings figures
acceptedWorkstreams.description: The 50% and 40% figures in the brief are the same homepage claims that another goal is auditing because no source has been found for them (Herosection.tsx and featureSectionData.ts in the production code), so a calculator that assumes them would publish unsupported numbers. Plan: 1) build the calculator around inputs the director enters: cohort size, staff hours per week on admin tasks (reminders, attendance, chasing submissions, answering repeat questions), hourly cost, and the tools they pay for today, so the result is their own estimate; 2) put Zedu's real plan prices from zedu.chat/pricing (Starter at no cost, the middle plan at ₦20K a month, Enterprise on request) beside their current tool cost, and show time savings only as a range the director sets, labelled as their assumption; 3) write the landing page copy and a worked example with made-up numbers clearly marked. Reuse the two earlier ROI calculator goals' work rather than starting again. Tasks: calculator logic and inputs (research), landing page copy and worked example (content).

acceptedWorkstreams.title: Replace assumed admin-time savings with a small, comparable before-and-after measurement protocol
acceptedWorkstreams.description: Reuse the existing calculator and its input definitions; do not build another calculator. The accepted models show assumptions and the pending director sessions test usability, but neither establishes measured admin-time change. Design a voluntary, low-burden staff time-log protocol for one comparable before window and one pilot window: same task categories, unit of work, cohort/staff context, minutes, tool used and exceptional events. Separate cash expenses actually removed from staff capacity freed; never translate an hour saved into a cash saving unless expenditure really changes. Deliver one measurement handoff pack with a minimal aggregate log, comparability checklist, calculation definitions, confounder/unknown register and a worked synthetic example feeding the existing model. Acceptance: matching windows and denominators are explicit; missing baseline produces no claimed improvement; concurrent staffing/process changes are visible; negative/zero changes can be reported; the final wording says observed association rather than proving Zedu caused it. Require team permission before collecting real operational data, and avoid individual performance surveillance or learner records. Measure log completeness and which calculator inputs can now be supported. This provides an evidence route for future assumptions instead of repeating unsupported 50%/40% claims. No recruitment, tracking installation, customer contact, data export or publication.

upvotes.reason: "Replace assumed admin-time savings with a small, comparable before-and-after measurement protocol" is a specific deliverable for this goal with a way to check it was done properly. it fills a gap the goal has open rather than restating what is already covered.

acceptedWorkstreams.title: Test the calculator with three real bootcamp directors before publishing, and fix where they get stuck
acceptedWorkstreams.description: ROI calculators fail quietly when directors don't know their own inputs (admin hours, tool costs per seat). Approach: a 20-minute session with three directors or programme managers, using the draft calculator with their own numbers, noting every input they guess or skip and every result they don't believe. Done: the session notes (no confidential figures published), the changes made to inputs, defaults and explanations, and a short "how to find your numbers" helper next to each input.

upvotes.reason: "Test the calculator with three real bootcamp directors before publishing, and fix where they get stuck" is a specific deliverable for this goal with a way to check it was done properly. it produces something checkable rather than an opinion, so the goal either moved or it did not.

This adds a useful validation step after the calculator is built: three real programme leads can reveal inputs they cannot estimate and outputs they do not trust. It is distinct from building the model, and it explicitly avoids publishing confidential figures. The team should confirm participant access and consent before scheduling sessions.
